title: Ziggy's Step-by-Step Surprise
markdown:
Ziggy blinked with rainbow colours and made silly whirr-click-pop sounds. Kian wanted to play Follow the Leader.

“Ziggy! Follow me!” Kian took a big step.

Ziggy zipped after him… bonk! Right into the comfy armchair. Oopsie.

“Oh dear,” said Grandma Nell, knitting. Click-clack went her needles.

Kian tried again. “Ziggy, turn left!” He wiggled his nose.

Ziggy spun around and crashed into the squishy cushions. Poof!

Puddle giggled. Ribbit-ribbit-heehee! “Ziggy’s like a bouncy ball!”

Kian frowned. “He’s not following me! He just bumps!”

Ziggy blinked slowly. Huh?

Grandma Nell sat on the sofa. Squeak! “Kian, when you build forts, you don’t just say, Build fort, do you?”

Kian tapped his tape measure. “No. I say, First, this blanket here. Then, that pillow on top. It’s like a special list!”

“Exactly!” Grandma Nell clapped. Pat-pat! “You give clear steps! Like a recipe! One tiny thing, then the next!”

Kian’s eyes popped wide. His smile came back. “Instructions! Ziggy needs instructions, not just follow me!”

Puddle bounced higher than a spring. “Instructions! Like telling Ziggy how to find yummy lily pads?”

“Maybe!” Kian giggled. He looked at Ziggy. Bloop! He held up one finger. “Ziggy. FORWARD one step.”

Ziggy’s lights glowed blue. Whirr-click! Ziggy took ONE careful step. He didn’t bump! He didn’t crash!

“He did it!” Kian shouted, dancing. “He followed my instruction! Ziggy, TURN RIGHT.”

Whirr-click-clack! Ziggy turned right, smooth as butter. He looked so clever.

“Hooray!” Puddle did a froggy jump. “Ziggy’s listening!”

Grandma Nell smiled her warm smile. “You’re giving him a plan, Kian. Each instruction tells him what to do. You’re telling him the story of where to go, one sentence at a time.”

Kian grinned. Two fingers. “Ziggy, FORWARD two steps!” Whirr-whirr-click! Ziggy marched. Then Kian pointed to a hoop. “Ziggy, HOP over!” Ziggy jumped. Boing-whizz! Right over!

Soon Kian and Puddle made a super-duper adventure. “Ziggy, left, right, forward, hop!” they called, laughing. Ziggy followed all their instructions. They invented Ziggy’s Amazing Obstacle Course. It was so fun.

“It’s like a secret code for Ziggy,” Kian said. “Each step tells him what to do.”

Grandma Nell hugged him. “That’s right, my clever Measure Master. Clear steps, like robot instructions. It’s how we tell machines — and each other — how to do things, step-by-step. It’s all about the plan.”

Ziggy blinked his rainbow lights, whizz-bloop-whizz, as if to say, I love plans.

“So giving Ziggy steps is like telling him a special story to follow?” Puddle asked.

Kian nodded, eyes sparkling. “A do-this-then-do-that story. And if we want him to do something new, we just give him a new story.”

The sun set orange and pink. Ziggy wasn’t just a wobbly robot. He was a friend who loved learning, and Kian was the best boy to teach him, one amazing step at a time. The hoop stayed on the rug for tomorrow. Grandma Nell’s needles clicked on. Puddle practised a hop of his own, which did not need instructions, being a frog.
characters: Kian (measure master), Puddle (frog), Grandma Nell (grandmother), Ziggy (robot)
author: StoryGen Community
